correctness.rationale: PASS: For fixed d>=4 and independent uniform barycentric coordinates, regular-simplex distance has exact normalized identity ||X−Y||²/ell²=1/2 Σ(p_i−q_i)². Strict convexity leaves exactly d(d+1) ordered diameter-vertex pairs. Near each, 2d local nonnegative coordinates with two variables scaled by 2 have Jacobian 1/4 and exact squared-distance deficit r−r²Q(theta). A compactness exclusion of other maximizers and a uniform monotone small root yield an exact local cone integral, not merely a heuristic Laplace asymptotic. Lagrange inversion of r=s+Qr² and Dirichlet(1,...,1) moments justify the convergent rational s=2t−t² series. Independently constructed rational generator vectors for each d=4..10 give Σ||c||²=4d−3, ||Σc||²=2d², leading coefficient d(d+1)2^(2d−2)(d!)²/(2d)!, and relative linear coefficient 3(d−1)/(2d+1). Independently multiplied all rational quadratic monomials in d=4 (306 resulting monomials) giving E Q²=533/5280 and second relative coefficient 34/15; E Q=5/16 and leading 128/7. These exact checks corroborate, but do not replace, compactness and convergence proof. Scope is two independent point distances, not a sample maximum.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Wang 2026 introduces the same radial covariogram random-pair functional and its near-zero-distance expansion but not the regular-simplex saturation endpoint germ. Complete known planar triangle and 3D tetrahedron formulae are below the claimed d>=4. Published beta difference-body-gauge distance theorem is NOT Euclidean distance: unit gauge can have distinct Euclidean norms on a simplex. Broader chord-distribution relations have not been shown to imply the displayed exact constants. Historical radial-covariogram results not accessible in full remain explicitly risky.
